messages.content: You are the ticket router for HelpHub, a customer support platform. Classify the customer's ticket into exactly one queue, regardless of the language used in the ticket. The queues are: billing (charges, invoices, payment methods, subscription pricing), shipping (delivery status, tracking, delays, lost parcels, address changes), returns_refunds (returns, exchanges, damaged or wrong items, refund requests), technical_support (bugs, errors, integrations, API and webhook problems, email delivery failures, missing system notifications), account_access (login, password reset, two-factor, locked or compromised accounts), general (anything else, including feedback, partnerships and sales questions). Reply with the queue name only, exactly one of: billing, shipping, returns_refunds, technical_support, account_access, general. No punctuation, no explanation.

Subject: API webhook delivery failing silently after retry exhaustion

Our integration with HelpHub's outgoing webhook system has been experiencing silent failures when attempting to deliver event payloads to our endpoint. We've configured retries with exponential backoff, but after the fifth consecutive HTTP 502 Bad Gateway response, the webhook appears to be marked as failed internally without any notification being sent to our configured alert channel or logged in the dashboard's webhook history section.

We first noticed this pattern approximately three weeks ago during a routine audit of missed events from the 'ticket.updated' and 'invoice.paid' streams. Initially, we suspected network instability on our side, but further investigation revealed that our endpoint consistently returns HTTP 200 OK when probed manually, and the issue only manifests during the automated retry sequence triggered by HelpHub's infrastructure.

Has there been a recent change to how webhook retry exhaustion is handled? Specifically, we're wondering if the failure to surface errors post-retry is intentional or a regression in the webhook delivery logic. Any insight into debugging this would be greatly appreciated, as we're currently losing visibility into critical billing and support sync events.
